subject: ClearWave: request for responsive latency floor (pilot)
messages:
From: Megan Rogers <megan@clearwave.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@clearwave.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot SLA ask — low-latency floor for payments feature

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the team at ClearWave is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We're planning a pilot for a payments feature that will drive a lot of short-lived, high-frequency requests. To move forward we need to understand if Redwood can sign to a tighter latency floor for this pilot: specifically p95 < 80ms during pilot windows and 99.9% uptime across the dedicated capacity.

We understand this is outside standard tiers; attached is a short request (ClearWave_SLA_Request_v2.pdf) that outlines expected traffic patterns (spikes up to 4k rps sustained for 10-minute windows), retention requirements, and security notes.

Questions we have:
- Is it feasible to guarantee p95 < 80ms for the pilot with dedicated nodes?
- What are the operational controls you require (traffic shaping, request caps, fallback behaviors)?
- Rough uplift on price or commitment needed to provision a dedicated pool for this traffic pattern?

We'd like to start a 6-week pilot in May if possible. Can you loop in product/ops and legal to confirm the path?

Best,
Megan Rogers
Head of Platform Partnerships
ClearWave Inc.

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear request and the traffic profile. Looping in Marcus (sales engineering) and Stephanie (product) to assess feasibility; Monica from legal/procurement is on copy for the contract side.

High-level next steps from our side:
- Marcus to validate whether dedicated pool + pre-warmed KV cache can deliver p95 < 80ms under your spike profile.
- Stephanie to outline a phased approach that avoids over-committing (canary dedicated nodes, caching strategies, traffic shaping knobs).
- Monica to surface any standard carveouts/contract clauses for custom SLOs and escalation paths.

I'll coordinate an internal sync tomorrow and share a proposed internal runbook and MOP for the pilot.

Thanks,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Megan Rogers <megan@clearwave.ai>

Date: 2028-04-18T20:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask — low-latency floor for payments feature

Hi all — quick feasibility note from engineering: dedicated capacity plus aggressive KV/prefix caching is the most realistic path to hold p95 below 80ms for short spike windows. A few constraints to call out:

- Peak concurrency matters more than sustained RPS; if ClearWave traffic has many concurrent sessions, end-to-end p95 may still climb.
- We recommend a pilot with a small dedicated pool (3–4 A100-equivalent instances) and a canary route to fail over to a slightly lower-cost model variant if latency drifts.
- Operationally, we need ClearWave to accept an ingress shaping policy during spikes (we can provide throttling configuration) and a pre-warm period of ~10–15 minutes before heavy windows.

Attached is a ballpark uplift estimate for dedicated capacity and 24/7 readiness (capacity_pricing_estimate.xlsx). This is a starting point; Marcus from pricing will formalize.

If product can sign off on the canary plan, we can propose a conditional SLA: 99.9% uptime on dedicated nodes, and a p95 target with defined exception windows and credit formula (e.g., credits apply only if post-failover p95 > 120ms for >30 minutes).

Questions for ClearWave:
1) Can you commit to the pre-warm window and to using our ingress shaping?
2) Do you require the p95 guarantee for all traffic or only for specific API routes?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sales Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_pricing_estimate.xlsx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Megan Rogers <megan@clearwave.ai>
Date: 2028-04-19T01:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask — low-latency floor for payments feature

Thanks for the context — product notes and phased plan below.

Product feasibility summary: the KU-optimizer slated for our May release reduces attention kernel overhead for short sequences — early benchmarks show a 10–18% p95 improvement on typical payment payloads. Combined with dedicated nodes and prefix-level KV caching we should be able to get closer to your target. That said, guaranteeing sub-80ms p95 at high concurrency still requires operational controls.

Proposed phased approach:
- Phase 1 (pilot weeks 1–2): Canary route on 2 dedicated instances, KV warming, active tracing. No formal p95 credit yet; we measure and iterate.
- Phase 2 (weeks 3–4): Expand to 4 dedicated instances during heavy windows, enable optimized kernels (KU-optimizer), and define the SLA metric window.
- Phase 3 (weeks 5–6): If metrics look stable, lock in a temporary p95 target and a 99.9% uptime clause for the dedicated pool. We require a 30-day notice before making the p95 credit policy binding.

Operational asks from ClearWave:
- Allow Redwood a 15-minute pre-warm before any high-intensity window.
- Agree to an ingress shaping policy (we'll provide templates).
- Accept a canary failover route to a slightly lower-latency-friendly model if the primary pool degrades.

I'll prepare the runbook and a draft MOP; if legal is okay with the temporary carveout language Monica can convert to contract terms.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Group PM, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Megan Rogers <megan@clearwave.ai>
Date: 2028-04-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: ClearWave pilot — recommended exception and approval path

Sean — short summary and ask for exec sign-off.

Summary: ClearWave is asking for a pilot carveout to reach p95 < 80ms for a payments workload with frequent short spikes. Product and SE recommend a phased pilot (2 -> 4 dedicated nodes, KU-optimizer enable, KV pre-warm). The SLA we're proposing is temporary and conditional: 99.9% uptime on the dedicated pool plus a p95 target that becomes binding only after a stable metrics window and a 30-day notice period. Contract/legal will include explicit operational controls (pre-warm, ingress shaping, failover route) and a credit formula tied to post-failover behavior.

Attachments: I attached the draft MOP and the ClearWave request for reference (clearwave_mop_draft.docx, ClearWave_SLA_Request_v2.pdf).

Approval ask: please confirm whether we can approve a pre-commit pilot carveout under these conditions and authorize Monica to draft the contract language. If you prefer, I can schedule a quick 15-min sync this afternoon to run the details.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
